All endpoints operate on servers you have already added to a project in the
hosted inspector. Managin

g API keys remains UI-only; see
[Not in the API yet](#not-in-the-api-yet).

## Base URL

```text theme={"theme":"css-varia

bles"}
https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1
```

The API is path-versioned. All routes on this page are relative to the base
URL ab

ove.

## Authentication

Every request needs an MCPJam API key in the `Authorization` header:

```bash theme={"theme":"cs
s-variables\"}\ncurl -X POST \\\n \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/servers/$SERVER_ID/tools\" \\\n -H \"Auth

orization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -d '{}'
```

### Creating a key

1. Ope
n [**Settings → API keys**](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys)\n in the hosted app (the card at the top of this page take

s you there
 directly).
2. Click **Create API key**, name it, and pick the **organization** it will act in.
3. Copy the key (

`sk_…`) immediately; **it is shown exactly once** and never
 stored by MCPJam in retrievable form.

Keys can be revoked from

the same page at any time. Revocation takes effect
immediately.

### Scope

A key is bound to one MCPJam organization at crea
tion and acts **as you,\ninside that organization**. Per-request authorization still applies: a call\nonly succeeds if the key's o

wner can access that project and server. A key
can never reach projects outside its organization.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Two delibera

te restrictions while in preview:
>
> * **API keys cannot manage API keys.** Requests to the key-management surface
> with an
`sk_…` bearer fail with `403 FORBIDDEN`. Create and revoke keys in\n> the UI.\n> * **Guest sessions cannot use the API.** Sign

in to create keys.

### Keep keys secret

Treat an API key like a password:

* Load it from an environment variable or secre
t manager; never commit it to\n source control or ship it in client-side code.\n* Scope keys narrowly: one key per integration, n
amed so you can tell them apart.\n* Rotate by creating a replacement key, switching traffic, then revoking the old one.\n* If a ke

y leaks, revoke it immediately in
 [**Settings → API keys**](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys).

If you see `401 UNAUT
HORIZED` with `details.reason: \"ORPHANED_KEY\"`, the key\nis no longer bound to an organization and cannot be used; create a new

key
from [Settings](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys).

## Conventions

**Requests.** Operations on servers are `POST
` with a JSON body (most accept\nan empty `{}`). **Reads**, the catalog listings and eval-run polling, are\n`GET` and take their o

ptions (`cursor`, `limit`, filters) as query
parameters.

**Responses.** Three envelope shapes, used consistently:

| Kind |

Shape |
| - | - |
| Single resource | The resource object directly |
| Collection | `{ "items": [...], "nextCursor": "...\
" }`; `nextCursor` omitted on the last page |\n| Error | `{ \"code\": \"...\", \"message\": \"...\", \"details\": {...} }` with a

matching HTTP status |

**Pagination.** Collections are cursor-based. Pass the previous response's
`nextCursor` as `cursor` in

the next request (body field on `POST` lists,
query parameter on `GET` lists). Cursors are opaque; don't parse them.

**Authori
ng vs running suites.** `POST /eval-suites` creates a runnable suite\n(the suite plus its test cases) **synchronously** and respon
ds `201` with the\n`suiteId`, WITHOUT running anything; author once, run later. `POST /eval-runs`\nis the async counterpart: it va
lidates and creates a run synchronously, then\ndetaches execution and responds `202` with a `runId`. Poll\n`GET /eval-runs/{runId}

` until `status` is `completed`, `failed`,
`cancelled`, or `timed_out`.

**IDs.** Every identifier the API takes is discoverabl
e through the API\nitself: `GET /projects` lists your projects, `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers`\nlists each project's servers,
and `GET /projects/{projectId}/eval-suites`\nlists its eval suites. Start from `GET /me` to confirm which account a key\nacts as.

## Errors

Errors always use the canonical body `{ code, message, details? }`. The `code`
is stable and machine-readable; `

message` is human-readable and may change;
`details` is an optional, unstructured bag.

| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
| - | - | -
|\n| `UNAUTHORIZED` | 401 | Missing, invalid, revoked, or orphaned key |\n| `OAUTH_REQUIRED` | 401 | The **target MCP server** nee
ds an OAuth grant; distinct from a bad key |\n| `AUTH_REQUIRED` | 403 | The **target MCP server** allowed the connection and asked
for sign-in on this call. `details.authChallenge` carries the parsed challenge. Your key is fine; see [Sign-in challenges](#sign-
in-challenges) |\n| `FORBIDDEN` | 403 | Key is valid but not allowed to do this, or the **target MCP server** rejected the credent
ials MCPJam presented (retrying with a different MCPJam key will not help; reconnect or re-authorize the server) |\n| `VALIDATION_
ERROR` | 400 | Malformed body or parameters |\n| `NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Unknown project, server, or resource |\n| `CONFLICT` | 409 |
The resource isn't in a state that accepts this write, such as a stale `expectedRevision`, a duplicate name, or an environment tha
t can't currently be launched. Re-read and retry |\n| `FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED` | 422 | The target server doesn't support this MCP c
apability |\n| `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | Too many requests; see [Rate limits](#rate-limits) |\n| `SERVER_UNREACHABLE` | 502 | Could n
ot connect to the target MCP server |\n| `TIMEOUT` | 504 | The target MCP server connected but didn't respond in time |\n| `INTERN

AL_ERROR` | 500 | Something failed on our side |

New error codes may be **added** over time; treat unknown codes as
non-retrya

ble failures unless the HTTP status says otherwise.

### Sign-in challenges

Some MCP servers allow the connection and ask for

sign-in only on a protected
call. The API never starts a sign-in. It reports the challenge instead:

* **HTTP 401 from the MCP
server** on `tools/call`: the API answers\n `403 AUTH_REQUIRED`. `details.authChallenge` carries the parsed challenge:\n its `s
ource` (`http_401`), and the `error`, `requiredScope`, and\n `resourceMetadataUrl` the server sent, when present.\n* **An `isErro
r` result carrying `_meta[\"mcp/www_authenticate\"]`** (the\n ChatGPT convention): the call succeeds, and the `CallToolResult` is
returned\n unchanged with an additive `authChallenge` field (`source:\n \"tool_result_meta\"`). A field the server already set
